name: Mixtures & Alligation
intro: **Run the §2 sanity check on every ratio you produce**: the mean sits closer to whichever ingredient dominates. If your ratio says otherwise, you read the cross straight instead of inverted.

qs.q: In what ratio must rice at ₹62/kg be mixed with rice at ₹72/kg so that the mixture is worth ₹64.50/kg?
qs.h: §2 — the difference computed on the dearer side belongs to the cheaper quantity.
qs.s: c = 62, d = 72, m = 64.5. d − m = 7.5, m − c = 2.5 ⟹ cheap : dear = 7.5 : 2.5 = 3 : 1. Check: 64.5 is close to 62, so there must be far more of the cheap variety ✓.

qs.q: Two varieties of sugar costing ₹28/kg and ₹40/kg are mixed in the ratio 5 : 3. Find the cost (in ₹) per kg of the mixture.
qs.h: §2 run forwards — this is a plain weighted average, no cross needed.

qs.q: In what ratio must water be mixed with milk costing ₹32/litre so that the seller gains 25% by selling the mixture at ₹32/litre? The ratio water : milk is 1 : k — find k.
qs.h: §4 — first convert the 25% gain into the effective CP of the mixture, then set c = 0 for water.

qs.q: In what ratio should pulses worth ₹15/kg and ₹20/kg be mixed to get a mixture worth ₹16.50/kg?
qs.h: §2 — the mean is much closer to 15, so the ₹15 variety must dominate heavily.

qs.q: 8 kg of a variety costing ₹40/kg is mixed with 12 kg of a variety costing ₹65/kg. Find the price (in ₹) per kg of the mixture.
qs.h: §2 forwards — total cost over total weight.

qs.q: How much water (in litres) must be added to 60 litres of a 20% acid solution to bring it down to 15%?
qs.h: §4, third worked example — water is 0%. The cross gives a ratio; the 60 litres anchors it.
qs.s: c = 0, d = 20, m = 15 ⟹ water : solution = 5 : 15 = 1 : 3. The solution is 60 litres = 3 parts ⟹ 1 part = 20 litres of water.

qs.q: A 30% alcohol solution is mixed with a 60% alcohol solution to obtain a 50% solution. The ratio is
qs.h: §4 — treat concentration exactly as you would a price.

qs.q: A 50-litre solution contains 8% salt. How much water (in litres) must evaporate so that the solution becomes 10% salt?
qs.h: §7, last worked example — the salt is unchanged. Anchor on the fixed component instead of using the cross.
qs.s: Salt = 4 litres and stays fixed. For salt to be 10%, total = 4/0.10 = 40 litres ⟹ evaporate 50 − 40 = 10.

qs.q: A vessel holds 80 litres of a milk–water mixture containing 12.5% water. How much milk must be added to reduce the water to 10% of the mixture?
qs.h: §7 — the water quantity never changes, so work out what total makes it 10%.
qs.s: Water = 10 litres and stays fixed. For water to be 10%, total = 100 ⟹ add 100 − 80 = 20 litres of milk.

qs.q: A milkman mixes water with milk costing ₹45/litre and sells the mixture at ₹45/litre, gaining 12.5%. How many litres of water does he use per 100 litres of milk?
qs.h: §4 — SP = CP of milk means the whole gain comes from the water. Get the water : milk ratio, then scale to 100.
qs.s: CP of mixture = 45/1.125 = 40. Water : Milk = (45 − 40) : 40 = 5 : 40 = 1 : 8 ⟹ 100 litres of milk needs 12.5 litres of water.

qs.q: A vessel contains 50 litres of pure milk. 10 litres are removed and replaced with water; this is done twice in all. Find the milk (in litres) remaining.
qs.h: §5 — final pure liquid = L(1 − x/L)ⁿ.

qs.q: From a cask of 64 litres of wine, 8 litres are drawn out and replaced by water. This is done three times in all. The ratio of wine to water in the cask is now
qs.h: §5 — compute the wine first, then subtract from 64 to get the water.
qs.s: Wine = 64 × (7/8)³ = 64 × 343/512 = 42.875. Water = 21.125. Ratio = 343 : 169. (Option (c) is the same numbers inverted — a common slip.)

qs.q: From 729 litres of pure milk, 243 litres are drawn off and replaced with water each time. After how many such operations is the milk down to 216 litres?
qs.h: §5, second worked example — the ratio will be a clean power. Find the factor per operation first.

qs.q: A container has 40 litres of milk. 4 litres are withdrawn and replaced by water, twice. Find the amount of water (in litres) in the final mixture.
qs.h: §5 — the formula gives the milk. The question asks for the water.

qs.q: A 20-litre vessel is full of pure spirit. 5 litres are removed and replaced with water; then 5 litres of the resulting mixture are removed and replaced with water. What fraction of the final mixture is spirit?
qs.h: §5 — as a ratio the formula reads ((L − x)/L)ⁿ, and no absolute volume is needed.

qs.q: A 90-litre mixture is 80% milk. 18 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced with water. Find the percentage of milk in the new mixture.
qs.h: §5, the variant at the end — apply the factor to the milk you actually have, not to the vessel's capacity.
qs.s: Milk initially = 72 litres. Removing 18 of 90 leaves the factor (90 − 18)/90 = 4/5, so milk = 72 × 4/5 = 57.6 ⟹ 57.6/90 = 64%. (Applying the factor to 90 instead of 72 is the trap.)

qs.q: Vessel A has milk : water = 5 : 1 and vessel B has milk : water = 3 : 2. In what ratio must A and B be mixed to get milk : water = 2 : 1?
qs.h: §7 — convert all three to milk fractions before touching the cross. Never put raw ratio numbers into it.

qs.q: A 60-litre mixture has milk and water in the ratio 7 : 3. How much water (in litres) must be added to make the ratio 3 : 2?
qs.h: §7, last worked example — the milk is fixed, so anchor on it.
qs.s: Milk = 42, water = 18. Milk is fixed; for a 3 : 2 ratio milk is 3/5 of the total ⟹ total = 70 ⟹ add 10 litres of water.

qs.q: Two vessels contain spirit and water: the first in the ratio 8 : 3, the second in the ratio 5 : 1. In what ratio must they be mixed to obtain spirit : water = 4 : 1?
qs.h: §7 — spirit fractions are 8/11, 5/6 and 4/5. The fractions are close together, so keep exact values, don't round.
qs.s: Spirit fractions: first = 8/11, second = 5/6, target = 4/5. d − m = 5/6 − 4/5 = 1/30; m − c = 4/5 − 8/11 = 4/55. first : second = (1/30) : (4/55) = 11 : 24. Check: 11 parts give spirit 8, water 3; 24 parts give spirit 20, water 4 ⟹ 28 : 7 = 4 : 1 ✓.

qs.q: 20 litres of a mixture with milk : water = 3 : 1 is mixed with 30 litres of a mixture with milk : water = 2 : 3. Find the percentage of milk in the result.
qs.h: §7 — total milk over total volume is faster here than the cross, since both quantities are given.

qs.q: A 40-litre mixture has milk : water = 3 : 2. How many litres of the mixture must be removed and replaced with pure milk so that milk : water becomes 4 : 1?
qs.h: §5 logic in reverse — the volume stays 40, so track the water, which only ever decreases.
qs.s: Water = 16 initially; total stays 40. For milk : water = 4 : 1, water must be 8 litres. Removing x litres of mixture removes 0.4x of water ⟹ 16 − 0.4x = 8 ⟹ x = 20.

qs.q: A man invests ₹12,000, part at 10% and the rest at 14%, earning 11.5% overall. Find the amount (in ₹) invested at 10%.
qs.h: §8, first worked example — interest rates are weighted by principal.

qs.q: A shopkeeper sells part of 100 kg of sugar at 12% profit and the rest at 20% profit, making 15% overall. The quantity sold at 20% profit is
qs.h: §8 — profit % is weighted by cost price. Note which branch of the cross belongs to which quantity.

qs.q: The average age of 40 students is 15 years. The boys average 16 and the girls average 12. Find the number of girls.
qs.h: §8, second worked example. Run the integer check on your answer.

qs.q: A trader buys 30 litres of oil at ₹80/litre and some quantity at ₹95/litre. He sells the whole lot at ₹99/litre, making 10% profit. The quantity bought at ₹95/litre is
qs.h: §8 — back out the CP of the mixture from the 10% profit, then alligate. The 30 litres anchors the ratio.

qs.q: A car covers a 5-hour journey partly at 40 km/h and partly at 60 km/h, averaging 46 km/h. For how many hours did it travel at 60 km/h?
qs.h: §3 — alligation on speed is legal only when weighted by time, and here the total given is a time.
qs.s: t₄₀ : t₆₀ = (60 − 46) : (46 − 40) = 14 : 6 = 7 : 3. Total 5 h = 10 parts ⟹ t₆₀ = 1.5 h. (Legal because the weights here are times, not distances.)

qs.q: Three varieties of tea costing ₹126, ₹135 and ₹175 per kg are mixed in the ratio 1 : 1 : 2. Find the cost (in ₹) per kg of the mixture.
qs.h: §6 — with the ratio already given, the weighted-average equation beats forcing the cross.

qs.q: In what ratio must pulses at ₹15/kg and ₹20/kg be mixed so that selling the mixture at ₹21.60/kg gives a 20% gain?
qs.h: §8 — the SP is a distractor until you convert it to the mixture's CP.

qs.q: A mixture of 80 litres contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How much milk (in litres) must be added so the ratio becomes 4 : 1?
qs.h: §7 — the water is the fixed component this time.
qs.s: Milk = 60, water = 20 and fixed. For 4 : 1, water is 1/5 of the total ⟹ total = 100 ⟹ add 20 litres of milk.

qs.q: A dishonest milkman sells milk at cost price but mixes in water and gains 25%. Water as a percentage of the mixture is
qs.h: §4 and the last row of the Traps table — "water : milk" and "water as a share of the mixture" are different numbers.
qs.s: Selling at CP with a 25% gain means water : milk = 1 : 4, so water is 1/5 = 20% of the mixture. (25% is the trap — that's water as a percentage of the *milk*.)

qs.q: A vessel contains liquids A and B in the ratio 7 : 5. When 9 litres of the mixture are drawn off and replaced with B, the ratio becomes 7 : 9. Find the initial quantity (in litres) of A.
qs.h: §5 conditions — the replacement liquid is B, not water, so the standard formula does not apply. Let the total be 12k and track each liquid.
qs.s: Let total = 12k, so A = 7k, B = 5k. Drawing 9 litres removes 9 × 7/12 = 21/4 of A and 9 × 5/12 = 15/4 of B, and 9 litres of B go back in. (7k − 21/4)/(5k + 21/4) = 7/9 ⟹ 63k − 189/4 = 35k + 147/4 ⟹ 28k = 84 ⟹ k = 3 ⟹ A = 21.

qs.q: Can 1 holds a mixture that is 25% water, can 2 holds one that is 50% water. How much should be taken from each to fill a 12-litre can with a mixture that is 40% water?
qs.h: §4 — alligate on the water percentage, then split the 12 litres in that ratio. Check which can gets which branch.
qs.s: Alligate on water: c = 25, d = 50, m = 40 ⟹ can 1 : can 2 = (50 − 40) : (40 − 25) = 10 : 15 = 2 : 3. Of 12 litres: 4.8 from can 1 and 7.2 from can 2. Check: water = 1.2 + 3.6 = 4.8 = 40% of 12 ✓.

qs.q: In what ratio must wheat at ₹24/kg be mixed with wheat at ₹36/kg to get a mixture worth ₹30.50/kg?
qs.h: Straight cross.

qs.q: A 27-litre vessel is full of pure milk. 9 litres are drawn off and replaced with water; this is done three times in all. Find the milk (in litres) remaining.
qs.h: Replacement formula.

qs.q: Two alloys contain gold and copper in the ratios 5 : 3 and 5 : 11. In what ratio must they be melted together to get an alloy with gold : copper = 5 : 7?
qs.h: Convert to gold fractions first.

qs.q: How much water (in litres) must be added to 24 litres of milk costing ₹32/litre so that the mixture costs ₹24/litre?
qs.h: Water = 0.
qs.s: c = 0, d = 32, m = 24 ⟹ water : milk = 8 : 24 = 1 : 3. Milk = 24 ⟹ water = 8.

qs.q: ₹1,600 is lent partly at 5% and partly at 8% simple interest, and the total annual interest is ₹104. The amount lent at 5% is
qs.h: Find the overall rate first.

qs.q: A 50-litre mixture of milk and water contains 20% water. How much milk (in litres) must be added so that water becomes 10% of the new mixture?
qs.h: The water is fixed.
qs.s: Water = 10 litres and fixed. For water to be 10%, total = 100 ⟹ add 50 litres of milk.

qs.q: A jar contains liquids A and B in the ratio 4 : 1. When 10 litres of the mixture is replaced with liquid B, the ratio becomes 2 : 3. The initial quantity of A was
qs.h: Replacement liquid is B — track each liquid separately.
qs.s: Total = 5k, A = 4k, B = k. Removing 10 litres takes out 8 of A and 2 of B, and 10 of B go back. (4k − 8)/(k + 8) = 2/3 ⟹ 12k − 24 = 2k + 16 ⟹ k = 4 ⟹ A = 16.

qs.q: A class of 48 averages 60 marks. The boys average 55 and the girls average 71. Find the number of girls.
qs.h: Alligation about 60, then the integer check.

qs.q: A container full of pure milk loses 20% of its contents, which is replaced by water, in each of two successive operations. The percentage of milk in the final mixture is
qs.h: Each operation multiplies the milk by the same factor.
qs.s: Each operation multiplies the milk by 0.8 ⟹ (0.8)² = 0.64.

qs.q: Sugar at ₹7.20/kg is mixed with sugar at ₹5.70/kg so that the mixture, sold at ₹7.20/kg, yields a 20% profit. The ratio of the ₹7.20 variety to the ₹5.70 variety is 1 : k. Find k.
qs.h: Convert the SP to the mixture's CP first.

audit: reading the cross straight instead of inverted
using the SP where the mixture's CP is needed
C2, C4
computing the pure liquid and forgetting the question asked for water
C6
applying the replacement factor to the vessel's capacity instead of the impure contents
putting raw ratio numbers into the cross instead of fractions
using the cross when anchoring on the fixed component is faster and safer
using the replacement formula where it does not apply
E5
alligating speed over distance rather than time
E3, M8
ignoring the integer check on a head count
F4
confusing "% of the mixture" with "% of the milk"
